doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: New York 1948: Tristano and the Miles nonet
title: The one-nighter at Birdland and the Bud Powell story
summary: Kirchner relays Sy Johnson's story of the nonet's one-nighter at Birdland opposite Tristano, with Bud Powell and Mulligan, and Konitz recalls playing in both bands.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: [Konitz asks Ken Kimery to hand him a picture from the shelf]
I’d like to see if you recognize this picture.
Oh, wow.
I think that’s Miles’ trumpet on the piano. I think one time we played opposite each other.
I’m going to tell you about this.
Okay.
Let’s do it now. Our Friend Sy Johnson tells me that in nineteen fifty the one other gig that the Birth of the Cool Band did was a one-nighter at Birdland.
One nighter, maybe.
Opposite the Tristano Sextet and you were the only guy playing in both bands. Does this sound at all familiar?
Yeah. I didn’t think it was a whole week.

Sy was there. He would’ve been about twenty years old at the time. Sy was there with a friend of his and he told me, apparently, that the Birth of the Cool Band that night had Bud Powell on piano. Do you remember this?
Kind of, yeah.
I’ll just keep going and stop me at any point.
Please. I’ve been waiting for this.

Sy tells me that apparently the last tune of the set was “Move” and they opened it up to feature Bud and apparently Bud was at the top of his game and just tore it up and the whole place went nuts. That ended the set but Bud, at that time as we know, already had mental issues. He’d already been hospitalized in a mental hospital and had gone through electro-shock therapy so everybody in the band except Bud got off the stand and Bud was just sitting there on the piano bench staring ahead, blank stare, nothing happening. So Sy said that at that moment Mulligan got up on the stand, kissed Bud on the lips, gently took him by the hand, and led him off the bandstand.
Wow.
Any of this sound familiar?
I’ve heard this story before. I don’t remember seeing it myself but I must’ve been there, anyway.

Yeah. My guess is that this [referring to the picture] was taken at Birdland and not the Royal Roost like the caption says: “The Royal Roost is a comparative newcomer to the club scene not aiming at glamour it offers the ultimate in Bebop to a youthful crowd.”
So what you’re talking about happened at the Royal Roost?
No, [it] happened at Birdland in nineteen fifty. According to Sy that was the one other gig that the band did live.
Okay so I’m right.
Does this jog any memories for you?
I just remembered feeling kind of good moving from Tristano’s band to the other band, just to be that active. I don’t think my union time was officially up yet after coming to New York.
The six months.
And here I was playing with two bands. I felt pretty good about that.
